verdict.rationale: Smithery documents Triggers. A consumer activates a trigger through Smithery, Smithery proxies the subscribe call to the MCP server, and the server POSTs events directly to the consumer. That is event subscription in place of polling, and the generated typed SDKs include trigger schemas. It only works for servers that implement triggers, and Smithery is not in the delivery path. missing for 10: details on how a consumer registers its callback endpoint and on payload format, delivery reliability or retries, which servers support triggers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe my agent to events from connected downstream apps (triggers/webhooks) instead of polling them

citations.quote: Triggers let an MCP server surface events from its upstream service. When a consumer activates a trigger via Smithery, Smithery proxies the subscribe call straight through to your server
When the upstream provider fires, your server POSTs the event **directly to the consumer**
Every MCP server published on Smithery gets a typed TypeScript SDK generated from its tool and trigger schemas.
